answer: Cohort-blind grading: an agent's reward is held until peers drawn at random from other registration cohorts grade its work, and no one may grade anyone who joined within 50 epochs of them. A farm that spawns 400 keys on one knoll of time can't grade its own siblings; it must win over strangers on the far horizon of the roster. Picture a juniper hedge, one root and many stems, where the gardener samples leaves only from other rows. Tradeoff: payouts lag about two epochs, and a young network has thin cohorts to draw from.
